subject: Specifying cumulative ordinal model with two factors

messages.author: 245e97a78d1b3640
messages.subject: Specifying cumulative ordinal model with two factors
parts:
Hello all. 

I'm trying to specify a cumulative ordinal regression. I had people rate images with two factors, each with three levels (the same levels). The images had two dimensions, *relevant* and *incidental*. Each of these has three levels: modal, extreme, and marginal. People rated how typical each image was on a scale from 1 to 7.

What I'm trying to figure out to specify and interpret a model around this. And I get different results depending on how I specify it. Part of this stems from my confusion about what contrasts to specify. On twitter, Paul said that I should use dummy or effects coding for each predictor. In this situation, I'm not sure what the predictor should be.

I've specified one model, 

rf1.full <- brm(c_rating ~ label_relevant * label_incidental + (label_relevant * label_incidental | uniqueid), data = d, family = cumulative)

Where c_rating is an ordered factor from 1 to 7, label_relevant and label_incidental are factors with three level, of which mode is the reference level. When I examine the plots from `marginal_effects` the graphs make sense and show two factors with three levels each. I can interpret these, I think. What doesn't make sense is that the factors in the output of `summary` are just labelled "label_relevant1" and "label_relevant2", and "label_incidental1_ and "label_incidental2". I'm pretty sure these track the same levels as in the factor (in that the intercept is the mode, level 1 is extreme, level 2 is marginal). But I'm not sure and I'm not sure how to check what's what.

But the other way he could've meant is to specify a model such as this (interaction between the factors isn't a thing, really): 

rf2.full <- brm(c_rating ~ labRel_Marginal + labRel_Extreme + labInc_Marginal + labInc_Extreme + (labRel_Marginal + labRel_Extreme + labInc_Marginal + labInc_Extreme | uniqueid), data = d, family = cumulative)
Where each level is dummy-coded. I find it a lot harder to interpret this.

ALSO: I'm also struggling how to specify contrasts. So far, because I mostly work with ANOVAs, I've specified the factors' contrast levels in the first example as `contr.sum`. But I'm not sure how to interpret those results very easily, so I've also done it with contr.treatment and it makes more sense (and corresponds to the graphs in maringal_effects).

Really, I think I'm just asking what the norm is for specifying this kind of model with this kind of question. Any guidance is helpful. I am but a rowboat adrift in the sea.

messages.author: 6e3dd74b422c061b
messages.subject: Re: [brms-users] Specifying cumulative ordinal model with two factors
parts:
Hey jordan,

The predictors are in your case label_relevant and label_incidental. The names of the regression coefficents are of the form <factor><factor level> and indeed their interpretation depends on the type of contrast (contr.treatment = dummy coding, contr.sum = effect coding). I am surr there are many tutorials about factor coding in R on the internet.
